answer: The guild of locksmiths files the pin code of every key it cuts, and no key opens a door unless its code matches the filed pattern. A shale key filed by an unlicensed cutter fails at once: at the crystal of the lock the pins must fall exactly as the guild record says, and a copied key lifts them wrong. Cutting a false key means stealing the guild's code book, bribing a locksmith and paying 9,700, and the quill entry in the guild file is read at every door, so a key whose code was never filed is turned away.
